slides.notes: TEMPLATE — “Pixel Picnic”, a playful toy-style deck. The cover is a scrapbook: a full-bleed 1941 carnival Kodachrome (Library of Congress, public domain) washed with the brand yellow, stickers slapped on top. Style family: saturated flats, hard sticker shadows (offset, zero blur), everything 2–4° askew, wobble loops. The blobs morph into the schedule tiles.

slides.notes: House rules as stickers. Count-up on the big number. Duplicate a card, rotate it ±3°, done.
The blobs morphed into schedule tiles — same ids as the cover shapes. A schedule that bounces beats a table that bores.

The photo-as-sticker recipe: a white frame rect with the ink outline + hard shadow, a photo with a soft ken-burns drift inside it, a marker caption, and one sticker slapped over the corner. Photo: Jack Delano’s 1941 state-fair Kodachrome (Library of Congress — public domain).
